description: SUM preserves its argument's INTEGER-ness, matching Snowflake: summing an INTEGER or NUMBER(p,0) column yields a whole number, so SUM(i)::VARCHAR is '13' and not '13.0', while a DECIMAL or FLOAT argument keeps a fractional result. The rule holds through GROUP BY, through DISTINCT, through an expression argument, over a WINDOW, and through arithmetic on the sum. An integer sum that OVERFLOWS a signed long is returned exactly - Snowflake's NUMBER(38,0) - so three times nine quintillion comes back as 27000000000000000000 rather than a wrapped or floated value. SUM over no rows is NULL. Converted 1:1 from query/SumTypePreservationTest (now retired); the Java asserted the boxed carrier with 'instanceof Long', which has no SQL surface, so the converted tests pin SYSTEM$TYPEOF (INTEGER where the Java demanded Long, FLOAT where it allowed a fractional one) beside the ::VARCHAR rendering that shows the same thing in the values.
